test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best defines globalisation in the context of economic reforms in India, post 1991?

options.text: Integration of the Indian economy with the global economy

solution:
The correct answer is __**Integration of the Indian economy with the global economy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Globalisation** refers to the process of integration and interaction between different economies, cultures, and populations worldwide, facilitated by advancements in trade, investment, and technology.
 
• In the context of **economic reforms in India post-1991**, globalisation primarily aimed at integrating the **Indian economy with the global economy**.
 
• The reforms encouraged foreign investment, reduced trade barriers, and promoted the opening up of Indian markets to international competition. This is a hallmark of globalisation.
 
• The **Economic Reforms of 1991**, often referred to as LPG reforms (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation), marked a paradigm shift in India’s economic policy by introducing policies that facilitated trade liberalisation, deregulation, and economic integration with the global market.
 
• Policies included reducing import tariffs, removing restrictions on foreign investments, and allowing multinational companies to operate in India, thereby increasing India’s participation in the **global trade and economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement-wise Analysis:**

 
 
• **Statement 1: Closure of multinational companies – Incorrect.** Globalisation promotes the entry and operation of multinational corporations (MNCs) in a country by facilitating ease of doing business and reducing trade barriers. It does not advocate the closure of MNCs.
 
• **Statement 2: Integration of the Indian economy with the global economy – Correct.** This is the fundamental principle of globalisation. It focuses on creating an interconnected global economy, fostering trade, investment, and exchange of resources between nations.
 
• **Statement 3: Restrictions on foreign investment – Incorrect.** Globalisation encourages foreign investment by reducing restrictions and creating a conducive environment for investors. The economic reforms of 1991 specifically aimed to attract foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• **Statement 4: Promoting only domestic trade – Incorrect.** Globalisation does not limit trade to the domestic level but rather emphasises international trade and interaction with the global economy.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Globalisation in India:**
 
 
• To increase **economic growth** by fostering foreign investment and trade.
 
• To integrate India into the **global supply chain**.
 
• To enhance the **competitiveness** of Indian industries on a global scale.
 
• To boost exports and improve the balance of payments.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Globalisation on India:**
 
 
• Introduction of **FDI (Foreign Direct Investment)** in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, and retail.
 
• Emergence of India as an **IT hub** and global outsourcing destination.
 
• Growth in the number of multinational companies operating in India.
 
• Increased competition, leading to improved **product quality and services**.
 
• Enhanced **employment opportunities** and technology transfer.
 
 
 
• **Key Policies Introduced During 1991 Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• Reduction of **custom duties** and tariffs on imports and exports.
 
• Dismantling of the **Licence Raj**, which reduced bureaucratic hurdles for businesses.
 
• Encouragement of private sector participation in industries previously reserved for the public sector.
 
• Introduction of the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)** in 1999, replacing the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), to facilitate international trade.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the World Trade Organization (WTO):**

 
 
• The WTO has played a crucial role in promoting globalisation by creating a framework for international trade and resolving trade disputes.
 
• India became a member of the **WTO in 1995**, which further facilitated its integration into the global economy.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Globalisation:**
 
 
• Unequal distribution of benefits, leading to **widening income inequality**.
 
• Increased vulnerability to **global economic crises**, such as the 2008 financial crisis.
 
• Threat to traditional industries due to **foreign competition**.
 
 
 
• **Notable Impacts of Globalisation in India:**
 
 
• The entry of global automobile brands like **Hyundai, Honda**, and **Toyota** into the Indian market.
 
• Growth of the **IT sector**, with companies like Infosys and Wipro becoming globally recognised.
 
• Expansion of **e-commerce giants** like Amazon and Walmart in India.
